## Goal

Translate keyboard input into game actions and render the shared game state in the terminal.

## Files

- `gridworld/controllers/controller.py`
- `gridworld/controllers/terminal_input.py`
- `gridworld/views/bash_render.py`

## Tasks

- Implement `Controller(input_source: InputSource)` and `TerminalInput`.
- Complete `BashRender`, keeping the supplied `refresh` method unchanged.
- Follow the supplied `InputSource` and `Renderer` interfaces so the launcher in S0-05 can connect these components.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The controller maps z/Z/ArrowUp to `north`, d/D/ArrowRight to `east`, s/S/ArrowDown to `south`, and q/Q/ArrowLeft to `west`.
- [ ] Space maps to `wait`; `Escape` and `:quit` map to `quit`; unknown keys map to `None`.
- [ ] `get_action()` reads the input source exactly once and preserves `None`. Controller receives an input source, not a renderer.
- [ ] `TerminalInput` preserves the space used for waiting and returns `:quit` on EOF or keyboard interruption.
- [ ] `state_to_string` converts terrain to `. # E`, overlays entities in order (`P` for the player, `?` for an unknown appearance), and includes `Turn: N` and the message, without printing or mutating the state.
- [ ] `update_render` calls conversion and then `refresh`, once each. Calling `close()` twice is harmless.

## Evidence

Record manual checks in a reviewed PR linked to this issue: key-to-action mappings, unknown keys, space preservation, terminal interruption and rendering `initial_state.json` without modifying it. These checks can be demonstrated independently of the complete game. Explain the separation between reading keys, translating actions and rendering state to the tutor at the start of S1.

Use manual checks in S0. Automated tests begin in S1.
Organize the work and peer reviews within your group.
